content: Ligand 1 is the trifluoromethyl probe on a cyclopentyl cap - joint-highest activity at 0.61, but the heavy cap holds QED to 0.819 so its Phi is well short of the bromine molecule. Atom 11 is the azine carbon bearing the trifluoromethyl at atom 12, a non-ring bond, and atom 20 is the cyclopentane CH. Anchoring on atom 11 lets me change the C4 group while the cap stays cyclopentyl, which means this episode cannot win on Phi whatever I put there - so I will use it for the reading I still want. Every C4 group that scored at the top is either a halogen, a heteroatom-bearing group, or an sp-carbon arm. A cyclopropyl is none of those: bulky like a bromine, entirely carbon, no lone pairs, no dipole, and roughly spherical rather than linear. If occupancy is really all that position wants, it should score with the leaders; if it falls back, then something about the electron density or the shape matters after all and 'just fill the space' is too simple a reading of the ten points I already have.
